methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a randomized, open-label, parallel-group phase II trial with a 3+3 safety run-in and 1:1 randomization (n=55 in randomized phase), appropriate for the question but with important limitations. The primary efficacy comparison is against a 15% historical control pCR rather than a direct randomized comparator (the protocol explicitly states 'No formal comparisons were made between the two experiment arms'), which introduces substantial susceptibility to selection and temporal bias. A sample size calculation is reported (25 patients, 80% power, two-sided α=0.1, 35% vs 15% pCR), but α=0.1 is lenient and the trial is underpowered for secondary EFS/RFS endpoints and biomarker subgroup analyses, as the authors acknowledge. Pathology was assessed by local pathologists at each site rather than by blinded central review, and allocation concealment details are not described. Statistical methods (Clopper-Pearson CIs, normal approximation binomial testing, Kaplan-Meier) are appropriate for the data types, though no multiplicity correction is applied across the two historical-control comparisons and no sensitivity analyses are reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is a prospective individual randomized phase II trial (NCT05009069) comparing two active immunotherapy arms after nCRT in LARC, qualifying as Oxford LoE 1b (albeit a smaller, lower-power RCT typical of signal-finding phase II work). Clinical relevance is high: LARC is a common disease, pCR is a recognized surrogate supported by the international consensus (ref 34) and Maas et al pooled analysis, and the pMMR/MSS enrichment addresses a population with limited ICI benefit. The 35.7% pCR with Atezo+Tira—if confirmed in phase III—could inform a new neoadjuvant strategy competitive with TNT (RAPIDO/PRODIGE 23 ~28% pCR) while avoiding additional chemotherapy, and the biomarker signals around PD-L1/TIGIT/PVR have translational implications for patient selection. Short follow-up (median 21.55 months) and small size prevent immediate practice-changing status.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard, and the manuscript addresses most key items: trial registration (NCT05009069), eligibility criteria, randomization, pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints, CONSORT flow diagram (Fig 1) with mITT/safety set reconciliation, baseline characteristics table, protocol deviation disclosure, and detailed AE grading per CTCAE v5.0. Omissions include limited detail on allocation concealment mechanism, no explicit statement that pathology was centrally reviewed (it was local), and no description of randomization method (stratification variables, block size, concealment). The blinded manuscript contains no data-availability statement, no code deposition reference, and no protocol/SAP sharing link—data availability must be scored low on what remains, though journal-stripped sections may partly account for this.

novelty_literature.justification: The combination novelty is genuine: this is, to the authors' knowledge, the first randomized trial of dual TIGIT + PD-L1 blockade (tiragolumab + atezolizumab) after nCRT specifically in LARC, extending CITYSCAPE (NSCLC) and MORPHEUS-Liver (HCC) precedents into a GI setting dominated by pMMR/MSS biology where ICIs have historically failed. Prior comparators (VOLTAGE-A, UNION, AVANA, R-IMMUNE, Xu et al sintilimab trial) tested anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 monotherapy with nCRT, so the TIGIT axis addition represents a meaningful mechanistic extension rather than replication. Novelty is bounded because the backbone concept (ICI + nCRT in rectal cancer) is well-established, pCR as endpoint is standard, and the single-arm historical-control framing limits the strength of the novel claim. The positioning section is well-grounded with appropriate comparators and does not over-claim.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear IMRaD structure, a quantitatively grounded self-contained abstract, and a discussion that systematically contextualizes findings against RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23, VOLTAGE-A, UNION, and CITYSCAPE. Methods clearly describe eligibility, treatment schedule, biomarker assays (SP263/SP410/CD155 with platforms), and analysis populations. Minor issues include awkward phrasings ('statistically improved the pCR rate'), occasional ambiguity around whether between-arm numerical comparisons are being implied despite the stated no-formal-comparison design, and figure/table captions are sparse (standalone interpretability would be aided by effect-size reporting in Table 2 caption). Limitations are explicitly acknowledged.

key_strengths: First randomized phase II trial of dual TIGIT + PD-L1 blockade (tiragolumab + atezolizumab) after nCRT in LARC, with primary endpoint met in combination arm (pCR 35.7%, P=.002 vs 15% historical)
Enriched for pMMR/MSS patients (100%), the population with greatest unmet ICI need, strengthening translational relevance
Pre-specified sample-size calculation, registered protocol (NCT05009069), ITT/mITT/safety set definitions, and CONSORT-style flow with transparent protocol-deviation disclosure
Manageable safety profile (grade 3-4 Atezo/Tira-related AEs 10.3%/11.5%; no treatment-emergent deaths) consistent with meta-analytic benchmarks
Well-contextualized discussion comparing favorably on pCR and toxicity against TNT regimens (RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23)
key_concerns: Primary efficacy inference rests on historical-control comparison with no formal between-arm randomized test, limiting causal attribution to the TIGIT component
Small sample (n=55 randomized), lenient α=0.1, short median follow-up (21.55 months), and no multiplicity correction across the two historical-control tests
Pathologic complete response assessed by local pathologists at each site rather than blinded central review, introducing potential detection bias on the primary endpoint
Randomization mechanism (stratification, block size, allocation concealment) is not described
No data-availability, code, or protocol-sharing statement present in the blinded manuscript; biomarker subgroup analyses are underpowered and exploratory
Single-country (China), five-center enrollment limits generalizability of baseline risk and surgical quality (e.g., 50-55% robotic surgery)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically competent, novel randomized phase II trial with a positive primary endpoint and clear translational signal, but constrained by historical-control framing, local pathology review, and short follow-up—placing it at the upper end of Tier 2 (e.g., Clinical Cancer Research / Nature Communications / JCO Precision Oncology caliber) with minor revisions to clarify randomization procedures, central-review status, and data-sharing posture.
